title: Microscopic and Elemental Characterization of Biosubstrates for Application in Biosensors
content: Biosensors are devices that measure chemical or biological reactions by producing signals correlated to the concentration of a specific analyte in reaction. To date, biosensors have been developed for forensic, environmental monitoring, food safety, and medical applications. Different sensing modalities require substrates suitable for anchoring active elements and enhancing measurable signals. Stability and biocompatibility are two of the most important and necessary characteristics of all types of biosensor substrates [1]. Some substrates must to be porous, have a homogeneous surface, or be semiconductors (e.g., plasmonic, enzymatic, or electrochemical biosensor substrates). Plasmonic metals, as well as organic and inorganic semiconductors, are widely used as substrates for these types of biosensors [2]. However, a recent trend is the use of organic and naturally derived materials because they are highly adaptable to the needs described and can reduce the generation of substances harmful to the environment.
